findings: The repository source preserves a linked-list duplicate-removal coding task and explicitly forbids Map/Set, but it does not say the list is sorted or whether duplicates should keep one copy versus remove every occurrence.

The candidate explicitly chooses the unsorted/remove-all-repeated-values interpretation, in-place relinking and acyclic-list assumptions as answer-side contracts, while explaining the keep-one and sorted-list variants.

The exact fenced Java contains no Map/Set types, equals the saved solution fixture, and passes seven named cases plus all 21,845 arrays of lengths 0..7 over four values against an independent frequency oracle under JDK 21.
The O(n^2) time/O(1) auxiliary-space tradeoff follows from the no-extra-set and no-sortedness contract; pointer invariants and deletion safety are explained directly.
